title: EPUB Ghost Spacing & OPF Errors: How to Fix Them
excerpt: Ghost spacing and OPF manifest errors are invisible formatting failures that get your EPUB rejected by Apple Books and Google Play. Here's exactly how to find and fix both.
meta_title: Fix EPUB Ghost Spacing and OPF Manifest Errors | BookKraft AI
meta_description: EPUB ghost spacing and OPF errors cause silent formatting failures on Apple Books and Kobo. Learn how to find and fix both problems in under 10 minutes.
html:
Your EPUB looks perfect in Calibre. It previews fine on your phone. Then Apple Books rejects it — or worse, it publishes but readers report broken formatting on certain devices. Ghost spacing and OPF manifest errors are usually why.

These two problems are invisible. You won't see them in Word, in Sigil, or even in the KDP previewer. But they're sitting inside your file, and stricter platforms will catch them every time.

What Is EPUB Ghost Spacing?

Ghost spacing is what you get when automated converters try to preserve your original Word or Google Docs formatting. To do it, tools like Calibre and Google Docs export inject thousands of empty HTML tags into your file.

Instead of clean paragraph spacing, your EPUB ends up with markup that looks like this:

<p><span style="margin:0;padding:0"></span></p>
<p><br/></p>
<p> </p>

On screen, you see a normal gap between paragraphs. Inside the file, there are 12 layers of empty tags creating that gap. Multiply that by 300 pages and your EPUB has tens of thousands of ghost elements that serve no purpose.

Apple Books and Google Play Books parse the full structure before rendering. When they find this kind of bloat, they flag the file as poorly formed — and reject it.

What Are OPF Manifest Errors?

The OPF file (usually content.opf or package.opf) is the manifest that tells reading systems what's in your EPUB — every chapter file, every image, every CSS file.

OPF errors fall into a few categories:

  • Missing items: A file exists in your EPUB but isn't listed in the manifest. The file gets ignored.
  • Dead references: The manifest lists a file that doesn't exist. Validation fails immediately.
  • Wrong media types: An image is listed as image/jpg instead of image/jpeg. Small typo, hard rejection.
  • Duplicate IDs: Two manifest items share the same ID attribute. Parsing breaks unpredictably.
  • Spine order errors: The reading order in the spine doesn't match the manifest. Chapters load out of sequence.

Most of these come from converting files manually or editing EPUBs in tools that don't update the manifest automatically when you rename or delete files.

How to Find Ghost Spacing in Your EPUB

The fastest way is to run your file through an EPUB Validator. A good validator will flag structural bloat alongside proper spec errors — you'll see exactly which files have ghost tag accumulation and how bad it is.

If you want to look manually, unzip your EPUB (rename to .zip, extract) and open a chapter HTML file in a text editor. Search for sequences of empty <p> and <span> tags. If you find more than a handful, you have a ghost spacing problem.

How to Fix EPUB Ghost Spacing

There are two approaches depending on how severe the problem is.

For mild cases: Open the affected chapter files in a text editor and use find-and-replace to remove empty paragraph tags. Search for <p></p> and <p> </p> and delete them. Also search for <span style=" and audit whether those inline spans are doing anything useful.

For severe cases: The cleanest fix is to go back to your manuscript, strip all formatting, and run it through a proper EPUB formatter that builds clean HTML from scratch instead of converting messy Word output. The EPUB Formatter at BookKraft AI does exactly this — it generates lean, valid EPUB 3.0 HTML without the ghost tag layers that converters add.

How to Fix OPF Manifest Errors

OPF errors require you to open the package file and check it manually, or use a validator that identifies the specific mismatch.

Run your EPUB through the EPUB Validator and check the OPF section of the report. It will tell you:

  • Which files are referenced but missing
  • Which files exist but aren't in the manifest
  • Any media type mismatches
  • Duplicate ID problems

Once you have the list, open content.opf in a text editor and fix each item. Make sure every file in your OEBPS or EPUB folder appears in the manifest with the correct media type, and that every manifest item points to a file that actually exists.

After editing, rezip the EPUB correctly (mimetype file must be first and uncompressed), run validation again, and confirm the errors are gone before uploading.

Why These Errors Matter More Than You Think

KDP is relatively forgiving. It accepts a wide range of EPUB quality because it converts your file to its own internal format anyway. Apple Books, Google Play Books, and Kobo are stricter because they render your EPUB directly. The same file can sail through KDP and get rejected everywhere else.

If you're publishing wide — not just Amazon — your EPUB needs to meet a higher standard. Ghost spacing and OPF errors are the two most common reasons wide distribution fails after KDP succeeds.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does ghost spacing affect how my book looks to readers?

Sometimes. On platforms that render it, readers may see extra blank lines between paragraphs or odd spacing that wasn't in your original manuscript. On platforms that reject the file, readers never see it at all.

Can I fix ghost spacing without rebuilding my whole EPUB?

Yes, for mild cases. If only a few chapter files are affected, editing those HTML files manually and repackaging is faster than a full rebuild. For books with heavy ghost spacing throughout, a rebuild from a clean source file is more reliable.

What's the correct media type for JPEG images in an EPUB?

Use image/jpeg — not image/jpg. The EPUB spec requires the full MIME type. image/jpg is not a registered MIME type and will cause validation failures on strict platforms.

Will fixing these errors change how my book looks on Kindle?

No. KDP converts your EPUB to its own format before delivering to Kindle devices, so the structural cleanup won't affect the Kindle reading experience.

How do I know if my EPUB passes Apple Books standards?

Run it through the BookKraft AI EPUB Validator before uploading anywhere. It checks the same structural rules that Apple Books uses for validation — you'll catch rejections before they happen.

Ghost spacing and OPF errors are fixable. The key is catching them before you upload, not after the rejection email arrives.
